sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by FRET imaging; receptor traffics to the cell surface and to lysosomes; JAK2 WT and V617F contexts both examined, confirming the tagged receptor is surface-expressed and responsive to signaling context.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 (same paper, PMC12380609) report a TOLLES-YPet FRET pair fused to the N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored TpoR. No residue number is stated, but TpoR has exactly one extracellular terminus — the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 26 after signal-peptide cleavage at position 25 (S|Q). The tag must therefore sit after residue 25 (insert_after_residue=25), giving residue_before=S and residue_after=Q. The junction is 468 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying the ≥3-residue constraint with wide margin. Full-length membrane-anchored TpoR with TOLLES-YPet FRET pair fused to its N-terminus (construct called SRAI-TpoR) expressed in mammalian cells; surface display confirmed by FRET imaging in the presence of JAK2 WT and JAK2 V617F.

sources.claim: We used a TOLLES-YPet FRET pair and fused it to the N-terminus of TpoR henceforth called SRAI-TpoR (Fig. 1A ).

Selective and efficient labeling of TPO-R extracellularly fused to a nonfluorescent, monomeric EGFP (mXFP) was achieved via anti-GFP nanobodies conjugated with Rho11 and Dy647, respectively ( Fig. 2 A ).

literature_notes: All three ledger clips (L1, L2, L3) describe N-terminal extracellular fusions to full-length membrane-anchored TpoR; none names a specific residue number. TpoR has a single-pass type I topology with a large extracellular domain (residues 26–493) and an intracellular C-terminus (514–635), so the mature N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at position 25) is the only extracellular terminus. No ledger clip supports any internal loop insertion or C-terminal extracellular tag. L1 and L2 are from the same paper and describe the same SRAI-TpoR construct; they are reported as one site. L3 is an independent paper and is reported as a second site at the same junction. No clips describe intracellular insertions or function-abrogating insertions for MPL.
